items.claimed: Yes-but-not-credited: Rule 5.137 requires storage connected to a net-metering system to be configured so the customer cannot receive net-metering compensation for electricity drawn from any source other than the net-metering system. Utilities may not interconnect storage in a way that lets non-NM electricity earn NM credit. So grid charging is not prohibited, but grid-charged energy that is exported earns no net-metering credit. 5.137 also applies to pre-existing (pre-2017) systems.

Consumer-owned utilities may cap NEB facilities at 100 kW unless they opt to allow up to <5 MW, may limit accounts to 10, and need not offer shared NEB (Ch. 313 §3(C)(4) and §3(E)).

items.claimed: Requires non-export: under the MPUC Advisory Ruling (Docket 2020-00332), a battery paired with an NEB facility needs controls that stop it charging from the grid. If it can grid-charge, controls must stop it discharging to the grid. Facilities >100 kW with storage must file a yearly attestation. Removing the controls ends NEB eligibility and credits can be clawed back (CMP and Versant NEB agreements/applications). Ch. 324 §10 requires an ESS form stating the charging mode (grid only / unrestricted / restricted / ICGF only).
